questions.title: Question 6: A loop that steps by 3 (8 marks)
questions.prompt: Determine T(n), with every constant set to 1, for `tot = 0; c = 1; while (c <= n) { tot = tot + c; c = c + 3; }`. Work out the number of steps for `n = 10` and give the Big-O. (8 marks)

steps.title: Count the passes
steps.body: The values of `c` are 1, 4, 7, 10, so for `n = 10` the body runs `k = 4` times. (2 marks)

steps.title: Count each line
steps.body: `tot = 0` and `c = 1` run once each; the condition runs `k + 1 = 5` times; `tot = tot + c` and `c = c + 3` run 4 times each. T = 1 + 1 + 5 + 4 + 4 = 15. (4 marks)

steps.title: Big-O
steps.body: In general `k` is about `n / 3`, so T(n) is about `n + 3`: proportional to `n`. (2 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** 15 steps for `n = 10`; the growth is **O(n)**. A constant step changes only the coefficient.

questions.title: Question 7: The nested loop for n = 3 (8 marks)
questions.prompt: For the lecture's nested loop (`c = 1; while (c <= n) { i = 1; while (i <= n) { print i; i = i + 1; } c = c + 1; }`), state how many times each of the seven lines runs for `n = 3`, the total with every constant set to 1, and the Big-O. (8 marks)

steps.title: The counts
steps.body: `c = 1` once (1); the outer condition `n + 1` (4); `i = 1` `n` times (3); the inner condition `n(n + 1)` (12); `print i` `n x n` (9); `i = i + 1` `n x n` (9); `c = c + 1` `n` times (3). (5 marks)

steps.title: Big-O
steps.body: The dominant term is `3n^2`, so the Big-O is O(n^2). (1 mark)

questions.title: Question 8: An iterative n! (6 marks)
questions.prompt: Write an iterative algorithm for `n!` and derive its time complexity, setting every constant to 1. (6 marks)

steps.title: The algorithm
steps.body: `long f = 1; for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++) { f = f * i; } return f;`. (2 marks)

steps.title: The count
steps.body: `f = 1` once; `i = 2` once; the condition `i <= n` runs `n` times; `i++` and `f = f * i` run `n - 1` times each; the return runs once. T(n) = 1 + 1 + n + (n - 1) + (n - 1) + 1 = 3n + 1. (3 marks)

steps.title: Big-O
steps.body: The dominant term is `3n`, so the Big-O is O(n). (1 mark)

questions.title: Question 9: Comparing growth rates (6 marks)
questions.prompt: Algorithm X takes `5n + 20` steps and algorithm Y takes `n^2` steps. For which values of `n` is Y slower than X? Which is better for large inputs? (6 marks)

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.body: n = 7: X = 55 and Y = 49, so Y is still faster. n = 8: X = 60 and Y = 64, so Y is slower. (3 marks)

steps.title: Conclude
steps.body: Y is slower for every `n` from 8 onwards, and the gap grows. (1 mark)

steps.title: Explain
steps.body: X grows in proportion to `n` (linear) and Y in proportion to `n^2` (quadratic), so X is better for large inputs. For small `n` the constants decide, which is why growth rates are compared for large `n`. (2 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Y is slower from `n = 8`; X is better for large `n`.
